svg.text: Looking up a column: the log-link
A column of the lattice is a stack of floors, each with its own ring structure. The log-link carries the units of one floor into the additive log-shell of the floor above, so ⊠ below
becomes ⊞ above. Only the étale-like pillar Π_v stands unchanged through every floor.
observer on †: sees Π_v of the
floor below as its own; sees
the units of the floor below
only as log(O×) inside its own
no floor sees the ring of

O and log(O×), and the link
The log-shells of †HT, one per v ∈ V
I_v = (p*)⁻¹ · log(O×_{K_v}) ⊇ O_v inner disc: O_v outer disc: I_v, radius grows with μ_log
These are the Frobenius-like, holomorphic log-shells of the floor (0,0): the codomain of the log-link from
(0,−1). At a valuation of good reduction that is unramified the shell is O_v itself.
outline only: a type, not a set
Every chip names a data type of the toolkit (species ids of `iut species`, C structs of src/iut.h). All numbers are read from `iut walk`.
